clue.text: Fish head first for the end of a marine pilgrimage

definitions.text: the end of a marine pilgrimage

indicators.note: first tells us the headland word goes in front of the fish

parts.note: a head is a headland, which is also called a cape
the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to start with the fish's head, set among sailors on a seaborne pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pilgrim Fathers on the Mayflower first anchored off Cape Cod, in Massachusetts, in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower pilgrims made their first American landfall at this hooked peninsula.

clue.text: Singer dear to Italians goes round America

indicators.note: goes round tells us the Italian word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: caro is the Italian word for dear
US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A singer much loved in Italy touring the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor.

clue.text: One, to wit, hiding in tree that's fishy!

indicators.note: hiding in tells us the first pieces are concealed within the tree

parts.note: a pine is a coniferous tree
I is the Roman numeral for one
sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit

explanation.surface: Someone, as it happens, hiding up a tree and acting suspiciously.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to fish, from the Latin piscis.

clue.text: Sounds like a bloomer the miller made

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the flower's name is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: a cornflower is a blue-flowered plant, a bloomer in the sense of something that blooms

explanation.surface: A remark that something sounds like a blunder the miller committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is something in bloom, the cornflower.
explanation.definitionFit: A miller grinds grain into powdery starch such as maize starch used in thickening sauces.

clue.text: Provide costumes for The Ring in the opera house

parts.note: to dress actors is to provide them with costumes
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A wardrobe department kitting out Wagner's Ring cycle at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's cycle of operas but just means a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The first tier of seats above the stalls in a theatre, where evening wear was once expected.

clue.text: Many dislike Conservative getting in? Not a lot

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it stands for many

indicators.note: getting in tells us the party letter is put inside the word for dislike

parts.note: odium is strong dislike or hatred

explanation.surface: A question about whether a widely disliked Tory candidate will win an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A small token amount is a tiny quantity, the opposite of plenty.

clue.text: Thumbs up (we hear) is the saying

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so a thumb gives Tom

explanation.surface: Someone giving a thumbs-up and reporting what people are saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumbs' evokes Tom Thumb, giving TOM, written upwards. '(we hear)' reminds the solver that a mot is a remark, borrowed from French and said 'mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mot is a witty remark or pithy quip, as in bon mot.

clue.text: Olive for instance appears to decline, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells us a word is spoken to give a differently spelt one

parts.note: to droop is to sag or decline

explanation.surface: A question whether an olive appears to be wilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshy fruit with a single stone, as with plums, cherries and olives.

clue.text: Do without edges in colour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside tells us the swindle word goes round the edges word

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: An instruction to manage without borders in a picture's colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep purplish-red shade is a hue.

clue.text: Monkey Island doctor indisposed

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: On Monkey Island the doctor is sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A large West African baboon-like primate with a brightly coloured face.

clue.text: Coming up again the matter in Rome appears pressing

parts.note: res is the Latin word for thing or matter, as spoken in ancient Rome
pressing business is urgent business

explanation.surface: A news item about some issue in Rome resurfacing with new urgency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rising once more after a decline is enjoying a revival.

clue.text: Marriage in the old poor-house

explanation.surface: A wedding taking place in a former workhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding joins two people in wedlock; in Victorian Britain a union was a workhouse run jointly by several parishes for the destitute.

clue.text: Ask if father's got the boat inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letters sit within the words ask if, without their first letter

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Father, as in a priest's title

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether Dad has the boat stored indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing or sculling craft is a small type of vessel.

clue.text: Victorious result with gold for the one following

parts.note: a win or triumph is a success
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A winner's prize includes gold for whoever comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir or replacement is a person who comes after another in a role.

clue.text: The House furious about one provider of room service

parts.note: a legislative house such as the Commons is a chamber

indicators.note: about tells us the anger word goes around the numeral

parts.note: mad means angry or furious
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Parliament is enraged about a hotel worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel maid cleans and tidies the bedrooms.

clue.text: Belonging to a church no bird gets into trouble in Kent resort

indicators.note: in tells us the run of pieces is placed inside the resort's name

parts.note: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, south-east England
taken as written
mina is a variant spelling of myna, a talking bird

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of the word into are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird gets into difficulties at a church in a Kentish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the clue word 'into'; 'gets' is only a link. Deal is a seaside town on the Kent coast of south-east England, and mina is an old spelling of the myna bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a particular sect or branch of the Christian faith.

clue.text: Two tins are knocked about on the road

indicators.note: knocked about suggests the letters are battered into a new order
two tells us to take the word for tins twice

parts.note: a tin is a can, one of the tins

explanation.surface: Two cans rattling along a road after being kicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from place to place, as a wandering pedlar or tramp does.

clue.text: Mangy flower?

explanation.surface: A question whether a flower looks scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means scabby or itchy with sores; the noun is a blue-flowered plant once thought to cure skin complaints.

clue.text: To catch connexion between banks is some game!

parts.note: to contract an illness is to catch it
a bridge connects the two banks of a river; connexion is an old spelling of connection

explanation.surface: An angler trying to hook something from a bridge spanning a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The most popular form of the partnership card pastime in which players bid tricks.

clue.text: Capital set-up in firm covering Asia, but losing capital

indicators.note: covering tells us, in a down clue, the firm sits above the next piece
in a down clue set-up means the word is lifted to read upwards

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: losing capital means the continent's name drops its initial capital letter

explanation.surface: A capital-city investment firm with Asian interests losing its money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second means the opening capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the chief city and seat of government of Cyprus.

clue.text: Airborne car — one brought the Duke of Plaza-Toro

definitions.text: one brought the Duke of Plaza-Toro

explanation.surface: A cable car carrying an operetta's comic nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Plaza-Toro arrives in Venice by water in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Gondoliers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin slung from an aerial cableway; also the Venetian boat that brought the Duke in The Gondoliers.

clue.text: Birdie sort of hole?

explanation.surface: A golfer's birdie at a curious hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A dove-like bird of town squares; and the first part of the word for a small compartment in a desk.

clue.text: Conversely the little beast can always be a pirate

indicators.note: conversely tells us the young animal's word is turned the other way round

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, a little beast
taken as written
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A remark that a small animal can, on the contrary, always turn pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea rover who raided Spanish shipping in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Cockney's cry of chestnuts he has to distribute

parts.note: the London street vendor's call for roasted chestnuts was all hot

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the h at the start of words, so hot loses its first letter

parts.note: the London street vendor's call for roasted chestnuts was all hot

explanation.surface: A London chestnut seller crying his wares and handing them out.
explanation.walkthrough: Street sellers of roast chestnuts cried 'All hot!'; a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the H. 'he has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out or apportion portions among people.

clue.text: In Endless Night — French painting by Sickert

parts.note: en is the French for in, as the dash and French signal

indicators.note: endless tells us the French word for night loses its final letter

parts.note: nuit is the French word for night

explanation.surface: A mystery title, Endless Night, followed by a French painting by an English artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both pieces: EN (in) and NUIT (night) with 'Endless' cutting its last letter. Walter Sickert, an English painter, made a famous picture with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert's well-known canvas of a bored couple in a stuffy room bears this title.

clue.text: River and take bird

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A list of things seen on a nature walk: a river, a lake and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird, also used for the water ousel or dipper.

clue.text: Would this other bird's distress appal Hero?

indicators.note: distress suggests the letters of appal Hero are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A question whether this bird's plight would horrify some hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading shorebird with lobed toes, an example of a feathered creature.

clue.text: Confused type of bird

explanation.surface: A muddled kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, jumbled type that has fallen into disorder; also the magpie, an old name for the black-and-white bird.

clue.text: Country house let out in washington

parts.note: a seat is a large country house of a landed family

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of let are put out of order

explanation.surface: A country mansion being rented out in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the state in the Pacific north-west, not the capital city the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of the Pacific north-western state, on Puget Sound.

clue.text: How many go off the rails?

definitions.text: How many go off the rails?

parts.words: How many go off the rails?
parts.note: reads as a question about people going wild, but describes passengers stepping down from a railway carriage

explanation.definitionFit: To leave a railway carriage at the end of a journey is to alight from it.
